summary: Tested new Claude Haiku 4.5 AI integration (public chat SSE + admin draft-reply) end-to-end. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_ai_chat.py with 7 tests — 7/7 pass (12.6s). Covers: (1) validation caps (message>2000 -> 422, session_id<8 -> 422), (2) multi-turn memory in same session (turn 1 asked services in FR — got streamed list starting 'Dédouanement (déclarations import/export...)'; turn 2 asked 'Quel etait le premier service que tu as cite ?' — answer correctly said 'Le premier service que j'ai cité était le dédouanement'), history endpoint returns exactly 4 messages [user, assistant, user, assistant] in order, no markdown ** leaked, SSE headers correct (text/event-stream) and stream ends with [DONE]. (3) English lang param — 'What services do you offer?' with lang=en produced English answer with 'the/we/our' tokens dominating over French tokens. (4) /api/admin/draft-reply/{id} requires Bearer (401 without), bad ObjectId -> 404, valid msg -> streams a French professional email (~625 chars) containing 'GLS' and French salutations, ends with [DONE], no markdown. FRONTEND: Homepage ChatWidget verified — chat-toggle at y=748 correctly ABOVE whatsapp-button at y=820 (both visible); panel opens with FR welcome bubble; sent 'Quels sont vos services ?' -> assistant bubble grew progressively (610 chars, growth=True) with plain text (no **); follow-up 'Quel etait le premier service...' -> got contextual answer 'Le premier service que j'ai cité était le dédouanement...' proving memory works end-to-end via UI; page reload + reopen restored the 4 bubbles from sessionStorage + /api/chat/history. Switched to EN — panel header became 'GLS Assistant / AI-powered — instant answers', welcome in English, and 'What are your services?' produced an English answer starting 'Hello! GLS offers a complete range of customs and logistics services'. ADMIN DraftReply: logged in, selected TEST_Pytest User message, 'Réponse assistée par IA' section visible with admin-draft-btn ('Rédiger une réponse (IA)'); click -> admin-draft-text streamed progressively to 625 chars in French starting 'Nous vous remercions pour votre message...'; admin-draft-copy and admin-draft-mailto appeared; mailto href starts with 'mailto:' (len 993), decoded body param matches the draft; button text switched to 'Régénérer' — click cleared textarea then produced a NEW 703-char draft (differs from first). Regression light: WhatsApp floating button still visible & un-overlapped, admin login with GlsAdmin2019! still works, contact create + list + delete work (used by draft test).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py public_chat replays only last 10 messages into system prompt as HISTORY string — fine for now, but if a session grows long the assistant will lose earlier context (silent). Consider summarising older turns if this widget is opened for long sessions.

server.py public_chat has NO rate-limit-safe recovery when LLM errors mid-stream: it emits {error:true} then still writes empty assistant to history only if text is non-empty (good), but the user-side bubble stays empty in UI unless the fallback branch runs. Not critical since ChatWidget shows t.chat.error on network failure.

ChatWidget.jsx: history fetch triggers only on first open (`loaded` gate). If the same panel is opened, closed, and the user comes back after a fresh login on another tab, staleness is possible. Acceptable for MVP.

DraftReply.jsx: no abort controller — clicking Régénérer while a previous stream is still running will race two readers into the same setDraft. Low risk (button disables on `loading`), but if `loading` is missed due to a delayed error, both streams could interleave. Consider AbortController.

server.py draft_reply session_id uses `int(time.time())` — fine for uniqueness, but if the admin double-clicks within the same second, two LlmChat sessions collide on session_id. Not user-visible; each request opens its own stream.

GLS_KNOWLEDGE system prompt is only in French but is used for both FR and EN answers with only a trailing 'Answer in English.' directive. The LLM handled it correctly in tests, but a fully English variant would be more robust long-term.

context_for_next_testing_agent: AI test file /app/backend/tests/test_ai_chat.py uses ~4 LLM calls per full run (~12s). Each request sets a unique X-Forwarded-For to avoid the 15/min per-IP rate-limiter on /api/chat and 10/5min on /api/admin/draft-reply. Chat history for a session persists in db.chat_messages — tests use random session ids to avoid collision. Frontend ChatWidget stores session id in sessionStorage under key 'gls-chat-session', so a browser reload keeps the same session and /api/chat/history repopulates bubbles. Admin draft SSE endpoint requires Bearer, 404 on bad ObjectId (parse_oid raises 404), 401 without token. Rate limiters are in-memory: 'sudo supervisorctl restart backend' resets them.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Multi-turn memory works because server.py fetches the last 11 messages by created_at DESC, reverses to chronological, drops the last (the current turn already inserted just above the fetch), and injects them as HISTORIQUE into the system prompt. This was verified both via pytest (turn2 answer contains 'dédouan') and via live UI ('Le premier service que j'ai cité était le dédouanement').
